plans.hypothesis: If Darwin's erosion-rate argument holds, the time since the late Chalk (latest Cretaceous) is of order 300 million years, i.e. between 250 and 350 Ma.
plans.pass_criterion: The numeric age of the top of the Cretaceous (the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary) on the International Chronostratigraphic Chart lies between 250 and 350 Ma.
plans.fail_criterion: The age of the top of the Cretaceous is below 250 Ma or above 350 Ma. The chart gives about 66 Ma, which would be a refutation.
plans.interpretation: 'Latter part of the Secondary period' is read as the late Chalk, the Late Cretaceous, ending at the K–Pg boundary. 'Secondary' corresponds to the Mesozoic. The test compares Darwin's implied elapsed time with the chart's radiometrically calibrated boundary age. It tests the conclusion about elapsed time, not his erosion arithmetic.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart is the standard reference for numeric ages of stage and system boundaries. The fields used are the boundary age in Ma for the top of the Cretaceous and the base of the Upper Cretaceous.

plans.interpretation: 'Descended from several wild species' means multiple independent domestication origins from different species. The modern test is whether dog nuclear genomes are monophyletic relative to wolves, coyotes and jackals. Later gene flow between dogs and wolves is not counted as separate descent.

dataset.name: NCBI Datasets Genome: Canis lupus familiaris (taxon 9615)
dataset.why_it_fits: The page lists dog genome assemblies with downloadable FASTA and annotations. Wolf, coyote and jackal assemblies are available from the same portal for comparison.

plans.hypothesis: If all domestic pigeon breeds descend from Columba livia, breed genomes will nest inside the diversity of C. livia and not group with another Columba species.
plans.pass_criterion: In a whole-genome phylogeny, 100% of sampled domestic breeds fall within the C. livia clade, and no breed groups with another Columba species at bootstrap 90 or more.
plans.fail_criterion: Any domestic breed, or group of breeds, forms a clade with another Columba species that excludes C. livia, at bootstrap 90 or more.
plans.interpretation: 'Descended from the rock-pigeon and its geographical sub-species' means a single wild species of origin. This is tested as monophyly of domestic breeds with C. livia, relative to other Columba and other columbids.

dataset.name: NCBI Datasets Genome: Columba livia (taxon 8932)
dataset.why_it_fits: It lists rock pigeon and domestic pigeon assemblies with downloadable sequence files. Assemblies of other Columba species from the same portal serve as the outgroup comparison.

plans.hypothesis: If the Glacial period was simultaneous worldwide, dated glacial maxima in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres coincide within a small lag.
plans.pass_criterion: Not applicable: no single public dataset identified with certainty.
plans.fail_criterion: Not applicable.
plans.interpretation: The test needs a dated glacial-maximum chronology from several widely separated regions in both hemispheres. That requires combining multiple regional datasets, not one dataset.
plans.no_dataset_reason: The claim concerns timing across regions and hemispheres. No single dataset I could verify records synchronous glacial temperature in both hemispheres. A single global stack would only show global ice volume, not interhemispheric simultaneity, and I could not confirm a landing URL or DOI for a suitable paired record. I give null instead of a guessed identifier.

plans.hypothesis: If oceanic islands hold fewer species than equal-area continental regions, species richness is lower on oceanic islands than on continental regions of the same area.
plans.pass_criterion: Across area-matched bins, median native plant species richness on oceanic islands is at least 30% lower than on continental regions, with a one-sided Mann–Whitney p < 0.01.
plans.fail_criterion: Median richness on oceanic islands is not lower by at least 30% in area-matched bins, or the difference has p ≥ 0.05.
plans.interpretation: 'Species of all kinds' cannot be tested across all taxa in one dataset. This plan uses native vascular plant richness from regional checklists as a proxy. 'Equal continental areas' becomes area-matched bins. Oceanic islands are those flagged as never connected to a continent. Any residual dependence on physical conditions is not tested.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: University of Göttingen, Biodiversity, Macroecology and Biogeography
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT has regional plant checklists with area, geology/island type and native species counts, accessible through an R package. Richness is compared between oceanic island and mainland units in area bins.

plans.hypothesis: If northern species naturalise far more readily in the south, the number of European-native plants naturalised in Argentina and Australia greatly exceeds the number of southern-hemisphere-native plants naturalised in Europe.
plans.pass_criterion: The ratio of (European-native species naturalised in Argentina or Australia) to (Argentine- or Australian-native species naturalised in Europe) is at least 5, in the GloNAF naturalised flora lists.
plans.fail_criterion: The ratio is below 2.
plans.interpretation: 'Productions' and 'forms' are read as vascular plant species. 'Naturalised' follows GloNAF's naturalised status. 'La Plata' is read as Argentina (and Uruguay), 'southern forms' as species native to the southern hemisphere. The ratio is computed against European countries' naturalised lists. Native ranges are matched using a standard checklist.

dataset.name: Global Naturalized Alien Flora (GloNAF)
dataset.why_it_fits: GloNAF lists naturalised alien plant taxa by region. The fields used are taxon, region and naturalisation status; native range comes from a linked checklist.

plans.hypothesis: If bats occur on almost every island and remote islands have endemic bats, most oceanic island groups have a native bat and most remote groups have an endemic bat.
plans.pass_criterion: At least 75% of a predefined set of oceanic island groups have at least one native bat species, and at least 50% of the groups more than 1,000 km from a continent have at least one endemic bat species or subspecies.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of oceanic island groups have a native bat, or fewer than 25% of the remote groups have an endemic bat.
plans.interpretation: 'Almost every island' is read as at least 75% of oceanic island groups (for example Hawaii, Azores, Canaries, Galápagos, Mascarenes, Fiji, Samoa, Tristan, St Helena). 'Often endemic' is read as at least half of remote groups. Subspecies endemism is counted since Darwin did not distinguish it.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
dataset.publisher: International Union for Conservation of Nature
dataset.why_it_fits: The Red List has range polygons and country/island distributions for all assessed bat species, with native/introduced codes and endemism information.

plans.hypothesis: If the human stature curve has the stated shape, mean growth velocity is very high in infancy, roughly steady in childhood, peaks in the teens, and falls near zero at adulthood.
plans.pass_criterion: Using mean measured stature by age from NHANES body measures: velocity at age 0–1 exceeds velocity at ages 4–8 by at least 2×; velocity at ages 4–8 stays within 4–8 cm/yr; the maximum velocity at ages 10–15 exceeds the ages 6–9 mean by at least 20%; and velocity after age 18 is below 1 cm/yr.
plans.fail_criterion: Any of these conditions fails, in particular if no adolescent velocity peak exceeds the childhood mean by at least 20%, or if the childhood velocity is not between 4 and 8 cm/yr.
plans.interpretation: Thompson's curve describes individual longitudinal growth. NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is estimated from differences between smoothed mean stature at successive ages, separately by sex. This blurs the individual timing of the pubertal spurt, so the peak is expected to be damped.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US National Center for Health Statistics, CDC
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES body measures files have measured standing height and recumbent length with age and sex, and survey weights. These fields give mean stature by age.

plans.hypothesis: If perissodactyls are closer to hares and rabbits than to other ungulates, divergence-time data will show the Perissodactyla–Leporidae common ancestor is more recent than the Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla one.
plans.pass_criterion: TimeTree gives a median divergence time for Perissodactyla–Leporidae that is younger than that for Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla, and Leporidae are closer to Perissodactyla than to Rodentia.
plans.fail_criterion: The Perissodactyla–Artiodactyla divergence is younger than the Perissodactyla–Leporidae one, or Leporidae are closer to Rodentia than to Perissodactyla.
plans.interpretation: 'Ungulates' is read as the sampled hoofed orders (Artiodactyla, with cetaceans nested within). 'Closer related' is read as a more recent common ancestor in a dated molecular tree. Thompson's evidence was the geometric transformation of skulls, so this tests his phylogenetic conclusion, not the geometry.

dataset.name: TimeTree – The Timescale of Life
dataset.why_it_fits: TimeTree gives pairwise divergence times between taxa, aggregated from published studies. The pairs (Perissodactyla, Leporidae), (Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla) and (Leporidae, Rodentia) are queried.

plans.hypothesis: If boys' and girls' growth velocity curves are similar in shape but differ in phase and amplitude, the female curve is closely matched by a time-shifted male curve, with the female adolescent acceleration earlier.
plans.pass_criterion: Female and male mean velocity curves (from NHANES, ages 4–18) correlate with r ≥ 0.8 after the best time shift. The female peak velocity age is 1.5–3 years earlier than the male one, and the peak amplitudes differ by at least 5%.
plans.fail_criterion: The best-shift correlation is below 0.6, or the female peak is not earlier than the male one.
plans.interpretation: 'Phase' is read as the age of peak velocity and take-off. 'Amplitude' is read as the peak velocity in cm/yr. NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is estimated by differencing smoothed mean stature by sex.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US National Center for Health Statistics, CDC
dataset.why_it_fits: Measured standing height with age and sex lets mean stature by age be computed separately for boys and girls, from which velocity curves are derived.

plans.hypothesis: If eggs are never oblate, no bird species has a typical egg wider than it is long.
plans.pass_criterion: Among species in the dataset, none has a mean egg breadth exceeding mean egg length by more than 2% (measurement tolerance), so the maximum species mean breadth/length ratio is at most 1.02.
plans.fail_criterion: Five or more species have a mean breadth/length ratio above 1.05, i.e. clearly oblate eggs.
plans.interpretation: 'Prolate' means length exceeds breadth. 'Oblate/discoidal' means breadth exceeds length. The test uses species-level mean egg dimensions (and ellipticity or asymmetry where given) from a published egg-shape dataset covering 955 species. Hard-shelled eggs of birds are the scope tested; reptile eggs are outside this dataset.

dataset.name: Data from: The evolution of egg shape in birds: Evolutionary constraints and adaptations
dataset.why_it_fits: The Dryad record has an egg shape file for 955 extant bird species plus oviduct, pelvis and phylogeny files. The egg length, breadth and shape-index fields are used to compute breadth/length ratios.

plans.hypothesis: If germ-cell chromosome numbers mostly lie between six and sixteen, most species have a haploid number between 6 and 16, with few species below 6 and fewer still above 16.
plans.pass_criterion: At least 70% of species in the Chromosome Counts Database have a haploid number n between 6 and 16, and the share with n > 16 is below 15% and below the share with n < 6.
plans.fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of species fall in 6–16, or more than 25% of species have n > 16.
plans.interpretation: 'Germ-nuclei' means gametes, so the haploid number n (half the diploid 2n where only 2n is given). 'Few' is read as under 15%. Polyploid taxa are included, since Thompson did not exclude them. The database mainly covers plants, so the test is on plants.

dataset.name: Chromosome Counts Database (CCDB)
dataset.why_it_fits: CCDB has downloadable records of gametic (n) and sporophytic (2n) chromosome counts by taxon, from which a per-species n can be derived.

plans.hypothesis: If weight varies as the cube of linear dimensions during growth, the log-log slope of weight against stature is about 3.
plans.pass_criterion: Across measured children aged 2–18 in NHANES, the OLS slope of ln(weight) on ln(stature), pooled by sex, lies between 2.7 and 3.3 with a 95% CI wholly inside 2.5–3.5.
plans.fail_criterion: The slope lies outside 2.5–3.5, or its point estimate is below 2.5 or above 3.5.
plans.interpretation: 'Weight' is measured body mass and 'linear dimension' is measured stature. 'Tends to vary as the cube' is read as an allometric exponent near 3. 'Not wholly' is allowed by the 2.7–3.3 band. Adolescent body composition changes may pull the exponent below 3.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US National Center for Health Statistics, CDC
dataset.why_it_fits: Body measures files give measured weight (kg), standing height (cm), age and sex per participant, enough for a log-log regression.

plans.hypothesis: If plaice weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 peaks near maturity, k as a function of length rises to a maximum near 30 cm and declines at larger sizes.
plans.pass_criterion: In DATRAS plaice records, the length class with maximum mean k = 100·W/L³ is between 25 and 35 cm, and k at that peak exceeds k at the smallest and largest 10% of lengths by at least 5%.
plans.fail_criterion: The peak of k is below 20 cm or above 40 cm, or k is monotonic with length (no decline above the peak).
plans.interpretation: k is Fulton's condition factor computed from individual weight and length. The peak is compared with the ~30 cm size at onset of maturity, which can be checked using the maturity field. Modern North Sea plaice mature at different sizes, so maturity is checked in the same data.

dataset.name: ICES DATRAS – Database of Trawl Surveys
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: DATRAS survey records (CA data) have individual species, length class, individual weight and maturity stage, enabling k and maturity-at-length for plaice (Pleuronectes platessa).

plans.hypothesis: If sunflower spirals intersect isogonally and orthogonally only rarely, measured crossing angles between the two spiral families are constant within a head and only a minority of heads show 90° crossings.
plans.pass_criterion: Not applicable: no verified public dataset.
plans.fail_criterion: Not applicable.
plans.interpretation: The test needs measured crossing angles between the two families of spirals (parastichies) in sunflower heads, with the fraction crossing at 90° versus other constant angles. That requires image-derived angle measurements from sunflower capitula.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I know of no public, citable dataset of measured parastichy crossing angles for sunflower discs that I can verify with a working landing URL or DOI. Raw floret-position datasets exist only in individual papers whose identifiers I could not confirm, and I will not invent one.

plans.hypothesis: If Arizona climate fluctuated with a regular period of almost exactly 150 years, century-smoothed Arizona pine ring-width chronologies spanning the last 500 years show a significant spectral peak at about 150 years.
plans.pass_criterion: In multitaper or maximum-entropy spectra of Arizona ponderosa pine ring-width chronologies covering 1500–1900 CE, a peak between 140 and 160 years is significant at 95% against a red-noise null, in at least two independent chronologies.
plans.fail_criterion: No spectral peak between 140 and 160 years is significant at 95% in any chronology, or the strongest significant peak lies outside 120–180 years.
plans.interpretation: 'Yellow pine' is read as ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa). 'Century-smoothed' becomes a 100-year smoother or detrending of standardized ring widths. 'Regular periodicity' is read as a statistically significant narrow spectral peak. The record is only about three cycles long, so low-frequency power is poorly resolved.

dataset.name: International Tree-Ring Data Bank (ITRDB)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
dataset.why_it_fits: ITRDB has downloadable ring-width measurement and chronology files by site and species, including Arizona Pinus ponderosa sites. The fields used are year and standardized ring-width index.

plans.hypothesis: If the biconcave red corpuscle is not a surface-tension equilibrium figure, its measured surface does not have constant mean curvature.
plans.pass_criterion: Not applicable: no verified public dataset.
plans.fail_criterion: Not applicable.
plans.interpretation: The test needs the measured three-dimensional profile of a biconcave red cell, to compute mean curvature over the surface and check whether it is constant. It would also require the shape change in diluted blood.
plans.no_dataset_reason: I could not identify a public dataset of red blood cell surface geometry (measured profiles or 3D scans) with a landing page and DOI that I could verify. Published profile tables sit inside individual papers. I give null instead of a guessed identifier.
